title: Unmeasured Database Indexing of Low-Cardinality Columns
damaged_code:
```sql
-- SQL
CREATE INDEX idx_user_gender ON users(gender); -- Only 2 or 3 distinct values
```
pattern: Creating a B-Tree or Hash index on columns with low-cardinality data (like boolean flags or status codes with very few distinct values).
why_bad: Query planners ignore indexes on low-cardinality columns because a sequential table scan is faster than index seek lookups. The index remains active, slowing down all insertions, updates, and deletes, while wasting storage memory [302].
detection: Database schema index definitions (`CREATE INDEX`) targeting boolean, status, or category columns where the total set of distinct values represents less than 5% of the total row count.
counterexample: Composite indexes where a low-cardinality column is combined with a high-cardinality column to filter specific queries efficiently. `Contextual`.
fix: Remove the low-cardinality index and let the query planner perform a sequential scan.
